chain.label: Company icing guidance permitted operations in freezing drizzle
chain.trigger: GOM section 8-9: "when light freezing rain, light or moderate freezing drizzle, or light, moderate or heavy snow is falling, aircraft may land"

chain.label: Flight released into forecast freezing drizzle at destination
chain.trigger: "The weather document indicated that the aviation routine weather reports for LBB were reporting IFR conditions with light freezing drizzle and mist and that the aviation terminal forecast expected the IFR conditions and light freezing drizzle to continue beyond the estimated time of arrival."

caused_by.evidence: "The flight followers who handled the accident flight's release and the dispatch manager indicated that the GOM contained no restriction that prevented ATR airplanes from operating in light freezing drizzle and light freezing rain."

chain.label: Airframe ice accretion on approach, outside certification envelope
chain.trigger: "beginning about 0432 when the aircraft was at 5000 feet msl, an increment in drag beyond the level expected for an uncontaminated airframe was again seen... by the time that the flap asymmetry occurred, a drag increase corresponding with about 23 percent of total power was present"

caused_by.evidence: "the airplane began to accumulate ice again when it descended into moderate icing conditions resulting from light freezing drizzle, a weather condition that was outside its icing certification envelope"

chain.label: Captain fatigued: circadian low plus cumulative sleep debt
chain.trigger: "due to the early morning hour of the accident flight and the captain's cumulative sleep debt, fatigue likely degraded the captain's performance"

chain.label: Flap asymmetry on selection of 15 degrees flaps
chain.trigger: "The FDR showed that a flap asymmetry had occurred in which the right flaps did not extend and the left flaps extended partially (8° to 10°)."

chain.label: Crew bypassed QRH flap procedure and go-around; captain troubleshot circuit breakers
chain.trigger: "after the captain commented about the flap problem, neither crewmember discussed a procedure or checklist to address it"; the captain "got out a flashlight and tried to troubleshoot the flap problem"

caused_by.evidence: "the captain's statement that the airplane had 'no flaps' indicates that he had sufficient information to recognize that he should immediately perform a go-around maneuver and apply the appropriate procedure from the QRH"

"the captain's repeated errors and decision to forego procedures might also reflect degradation from fatigue as a result of performing during a time when he was normally asleep, as well as performing with a sleep debt"

chain.label: Poor CRM: no plan communicated, first officer not assertive, steep authority gradient
chain.trigger: "the captain did not provide adequate leadership in response to the anomaly. Further, the first officer was not assertive in voicing her concerns"

caused_by.evidence: "the captain pursued his own plan of action without providing any guidance to the first officer or performing the duties required of him as the PM"

chain.label: Flight crew failed to monitor decaying airspeed
chain.trigger: "As the airspeed decayed, neither flight crewmember made any verbal reference about airspeed (actual or target), and at no time did the captain call out the localizer, glideslope, airspeed, or vertical speed deviations."

caused_by.evidence: "the captain's failure to call out the first officer's airspeed deviations resulted directly from his preoccupation with performing an inappropriate, nonstandard procedure in response to the flap anomaly"

"the first officer's failure to maintain airspeed while acting as the PF likely resulted from being distracted by the flap anomaly, the captain's actions in response to it, and the control force inputs needed to maintain aircraft control"
"the presence of icing conditions requires an increased awareness of the airspeed because of the detrimental effects that icing can have on aircraft performance"

chain.label: Captain decided to continue the unstabilized approach after stick shaker
chain.trigger: "the first officer asked, 'should I go around,' and the captain replied, 'no,' and then stated, 'keep descending.'"

caused_by.evidence: "Multiple cues existed that indicated the approach was unstabilized, including excessive deviation from the glidepath..., sink rate greater than 1,000 fpm, and airspeed less than the required approach speed."
"the captain's quick dismissal of the first officer's go-around inquiry likely discouraged the first officer from voicing her continued concerns and challenging the captain's decision"
"fatigue due to the time of day in which the accident occurred and a cumulative sleep debt, which likely impaired the captain's performance"

chain.label: Power reduced to 10 percent torque after stall and TAWS warnings
chain.trigger: "Procedures for responding to either the stick shaker or the TAWS warning require the immediate application of maximum engine power; however, 2 seconds later, the captain reduced the airplane's engine power to about 10 percent torque"

caused_by.evidence: "the captain's failure to immediately respond to the aural stall warning, the stick shaker, and the TAWS warning resulted in his inability to arrest the airplane's descent and avoid impact with the ground"
"As the captain continued the approach, the airspeed again decreased below the minimum safe approach speed."

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall at low altitude
chain.trigger: "the load factor stopped increasing about 1.12 Gs, indicating that an aerodynamic stall was imminent" at about 150 feet agl and 123 KIAS

caused_by.evidence: "At 0436:18, about 9 seconds before impact, the pilot began to pull back on the control column for several seconds. In response... the pitch attitude, AOA, and load factor all began increasing."
"The airspeed when the stall warning occurred was about 124 kts, approximately 19 kts below the minimum safe airspeed for the approach of 143 kts."

"the effects of ice on aircraft are cumulative; thrust is reduced, drag increases, lift lessens, and weight increases. The results are an increase in stall speed and a deterioration of aircraft performance."

chain.label: Uncommanded roll and oscillations until impact
chain.trigger: "the airplane experienced an uncommanded roll followed by a series of roll, yaw, and pitch oscillations, which continued until ground impact"

caused_by.evidence: "About 2 seconds after the stall warning occurred, the airplane experienced an uncommanded roll"; the captain "had no lateral control of the airplane and... the controls were almost 'snatched' out of his hands"

chain.label: Impact short of runway 17R and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: "the airplane initially impacted flat, grassy terrain about 300 feet north of the runway 17R blast pad"; "a fuel-fed fire erupted during the accident sequence"

caused_by.evidence: "The airplane then rolled left to a bank angle of 50° left-wing-down (LWD) bank, and then right reaching a 10° RWD bank before it impacted the ground."

chain.label: Captain seriously injured, first officer minor injuries
chain.trigger: "The captain sustained serious injuries, and the first officer sustained minor injuries. The airplane was substantially damaged."

caused_by.evidence: "The airplane was substantially damaged by the impact forces and postcrash fire."
